passage: Come, sit, Minakshi, and I'll tell you about the worst night of my first job, and why I'm so strict about rest now. I'm Afreen, and I was incident commander for a banking outage. By hour six the engineers were snapping at each other, and I saw one of them type the same command twice. I thought: tired minds make mistakes, and mine is one of them. So I stopped, called a break, and sent home the two who had been up since midnight to sleep. Fresh people took over, and I handed my notes to a colleague and rested for three hours myself. Some said I was wasting time. When I came back, the new team had found the fault in twenty minutes. Since then I plan handovers before an incident starts.

qa.q: What had one engineer done by hour six?
qa.a: One engineer had typed the same command twice.

qa.q: What was Afreen thinking when seeing the repeated command?
qa.a: Afreen was worried that tiredness was causing mistakes, including Afreen's own, which is why Afreen stopped everything.

qa.q: Which choice inside the story made the difference, and why?
qa.a: Calling a break and bringing in fresh people made the difference, since tired engineers were making mistakes and the new team found the fault in twenty minutes.

qa.q: How might the two engineers sent home have felt at first?
qa.a: They may have felt reluctant to leave in the middle of the crisis, but they were probably also relieved, having been up since midnight.

grounding: Shows a commander who, knowing tired minds make errors, rotates people and sends the first responders to sleep before returning.
